title: Biogeography
author: Wikipedia contributors
attribution: Wikipedia contributors, “Biogeography”, English Wikipedia. Text available under CC BY-SA 4.0; see source history for contributors.
paragraphs: Biogeography is the study of the distribution of species and ecosystems in geographic space and throughout geological time. Organisms and biological communities often vary in a regular fashion along geographic gradients of latitude, elevation, isolation and habitat area. Phytogeography is the branch of biogeography that studies the distribution of plants, Zoogeography is the branch that studies distribution of animals, while Mycogeography is the branch that studies distribution of fungi, such as mushrooms.

Knowledge of spatial variation in the numbers and types of organisms is as vital to us today as it was to our early human ancestors, as we adapt to heterogeneous but geographically predictable environments. Biogeography is an integrative field of inquiry that unites concepts and information from ecology, evolutionary biology, taxonomy, geology, physical geography, palaeontology, and climatology.

Modern biogeographic research combines information and ideas from many fields, from the physiological and ecological constraints on organismal dispersal to geological and climatological phenomena operating at global spatial scales and evolutionary time frames.

The short-term interactions within a habitat and species of organisms describe the ecological application of biogeography. Historical biogeography describes the long-term, evolutionary periods of time for broader classifications of organisms. Early scientists, beginning with Carl Linnaeus, contributed to the development of biogeography as a science.

The scientific theory of biogeography grows out of the work of Alexander von Humboldt (1769–1859), Francisco Jose de Caldas (1768–1816), Hewett Cottrell Watson (1804–1881), Alphonse de Candolle (1806–1893), Alfred Russel Wallace (1823–1913), Philip Lutley Sclater (1829–1913) and other biologists and explorers.

sentence.text: Knowledge of spatial variation in the numbers and types of organisms is as vital to us today as it was to our early human ancestors, as we adapt to heterogeneous but geographically predictable environments.
sentence.translation: 正如这类知识对早期人类祖先至关重要一样，了解生物数量和类型的空间差异对今天的我们同样重要，因为我们需要适应虽有差异、但在地理分布上具有可预测性的环境。
sentence.analysis: 主干是 Knowledge is as vital to us today as it was to our early human ancestors。主语的中心词 Knowledge 为不可数名词，所以谓语用 is；of spatial variation 及其后的 in 短语逐层限定知识的内容。as…as… 构成同级比较，表示“同样重要”，比较从句中的 it 指前面的 knowledge。最后一个 as 引导原因状语从句，表示“因为”，不同于前面的比较用法。but 连接 heterogeneous 和 geographically predictable，表达环境有差异却仍具有地理可预测性。

questions.prompt: 根据第一段和第二段，哪项最准确地概括了生物地理学？
options: 只研究一个地点当前的气温，不涉及生物分布
只记录植物的名称，不涉及动物或真菌
只比较动物数量，不考虑地理条件或历史变化
综合多个学科，研究物种与生态系统在空间及地质时间中的分布
questions.explanation: 第一段的定义同时包含 geographic space 和 geological time；第二段把该领域称为 integrative，并列出生态学、演化生物学、地质学等多个学科。因此它不是只处理某一种生物或单一时间尺度的学科。
hints: 找能覆盖所问范围的概括，排除只描述局部的选项。
回到第 1、2 段，逐项核对主体、范围及表示条件或程度的词。

questions.prompt: 根据第四段，历史生物地理学与文中提到的生态应用相比，更侧重什么？
options: 一个栖息地内当下的短期相互作用
完全忽略时间变化，只研究纬度差异
较长的演化时间尺度以及更广泛的生物分类群
只测量某一地点当天的物种数量
questions.explanation: 第四段先将 short-term interactions 与生态应用相联系，随后说明 historical biogeography 关注 long-term, evolutionary periods，以及 broader classifications of organisms。题目考查这两个研究侧重点的对照。
hints: 分别列出两个概念的特征，再比较相同点和不同点。
